messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — small-payload (avg ~30 tokens) latency regressions when switching to FlashAttention v3 on H100 in ap-southeast1. Seeing ~7-12% p95 increase vs Triton vendor kernel. Anyone else noticing this?
Samir Patel: Yep saw that on a quick run yesterday. Flashv3 wins for long seqs but microburst p95 goes up. Might be warmup/packing behavior.
Lina Gomez: Logs look like more frequent kernel launches and smaller block sizes. Could be packing thresholds + the new workspace layout in v3.
Jasper Holt: Quick repro attached — run bench with `--batch-size 8 --seq-len 32 --warmup 50`. Observed p95: 48ms (flashv3) vs 44ms (triton). Config snippet: 
```json
{"model":"llama-13b","quant":"q8_0","kernel":"flashv3","packs":true}
```
Maria Chen: deploy-bot: rolling canary deployed to ap-southeast1 with flashv3; attaching a couple traces from the first 1k requests.
Samir Patel: Hypothesis: flashv3 has a higher per-call setup cost that dominates for tiny payloads. Two mitigations: (1) lower selection hysteresis so runtime prefers Triton for small payloads, or (2) increase batching window for microbursts (adds latency but stabilizes p95).
Lina Gomez: Want concrete thresholds. My rough rule: if avg_seq_len < 50 and p95_delta_vs_triton > 5% => prefer vendor kernel. Flashv3 wins when avg_seq_len >= 128 or batch occupancy > 60%. Also factor quantization behavior.
Jasper Holt: Proposed routing playbook snippet: 
```text
# pseudo playbook
if avg_seq_len < 64 and p95_delta_vs_triton > 0.05:
  route->triton
elif cpu_util > 70% and avg_seq_len > 128:
  route->flashv3
else:
  default->triton
```
Maria Chen: On quantization: q8_0 seems to amplify variance for flashv3 at small batches. q8_1 looked more stable in earlier runs. Add quant-check to the decision matrix.
Samir Patel: Also consider driver/library differences per region. EU-west H100 on driver 535 looked fine; ap-southeast1 runs are on driver 540. We should sweep driver versions.
Lina Gomez: Action items: (1) run 5k-sample microburst bench across us-east1 / ap-southeast1 / eu-west1 on H100 with driver matrix; (2) add kernel fallback rule to runtime routing; (3) add CI perf test that simulates small payload microbursts.
Jasper Holt: I'll seed the bench and push a canary flag `--kernel-hysteresis-ms=30` to the runtime so we can observe behavior without full switchover.
Maria Chen: Thanks. @Samir can you own the driver sweep? @Lina please add the fallback rule PR and quant-check. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: On it. ETA EOD tomorrow.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed to 10% traffic in ap-southeast1 with flags: `--kernel-hysteresis-ms=30`.
Lina Gomez: PR opened: routing fallback + quant-check — https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4321
Jasper Holt: Bench command for reproducibility: `./bench/microburst_sweep.sh --seeds 42 --iters 1000 --kernels flashv3,triton --qtypes q8_0,q8_1`
Maria Chen: Good. We'll reconvene after the driver sweep results (expect ~24h). Logging this thread into the playbooks repo for next oncall.
Samir Patel: Noted. Will post CSVs + heatmaps to the bench bucket when done.
Lina Gomez: Thanks all — small-payload cases are important for search/snippets product. Keep the canary tight.
Jasper Holt: acknowledged.
Maria Chen: closing with a reminder: add a short perf note in the release notes if we keep flashv3 — mention microburst caveat and routing rule.
Samir Patel: will draft.
Maria Chen: 👍
